beats.text: It began with air mattresses in 2007.
beats.note: Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia rented out space in their San Francisco apartment during a design conference, charging $80 a night, to help pay their rent.
The site, airbedandbreakfast.com, launched on 11 August 2008. It was shortened to Airbnb in March 2009 to eliminate confusion over air mattresses.

beats.text: They sold political cereal at the 2008 conventions.
beats.note: Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's, sold mostly at the Democratic National Convention, according to Wikipedia. ProductHabits says roughly 500 boxes of each were made, planned at $40 a box.

beats.context: The sum reported as raised by selling cereal. Wikipedia, Benzinga and ProductHabits all give it, though none quotes the founders directly.

beats.text: Paul Graham doubted anyone would use it.
beats.note: ProductHabits says he was sceptical but backed the founders themselves. Y Combinator took them on in January 2009 for $20,000 and a 6 per cent stake, per Wikipedia.

beats.name: Airbnb
beats.role: The shortened name, by which point the site had 10,000 users and 2,500 listings, according to Wikipedia.
